The brief facts, as per the complaint filed by the  complainant, are as follows:-
 (a) Shri Prashant Malik, son of the revisionist got  married to respondent no.1 on 30.11.2010,
 according to Hindu customs and rights during  COVID-19 pandemic, in the presence of limited  number of guests and relatives.

During the marriage  ceremony, the revisionist being the eldest of the  family, in the presence of the respondents, entrusted  the respondents, diamond, gold and silver jewelries  approximately of Rs.8.00 Lakhs.

(b) In July, 2021 when the son of revisionist visited his  in-laws to take the respondent no.1 to her  matrimonial home, then, the respondent no.1 flatly  refused to accompany him on the ground that she  needs separate flat for residence.
In September  2021, the respondents sent goons to extend threat to  the revisionist for dire consequences, if Rs.28.00  Lakhs were not paid by them to the respondents.
In  this connection, NCR No. 38/2021, dated  17.10.2021 was lodged.

(c) On 05.10.2021, respondent no.1, from her mobile  number had confirmed to the mobile number of her Crl. Rev. No. 159/2023 Jagbir Singh Malik Vs. NCT of Delhi Page - 2 of 6  son that there was no dowry demand at the time of  marriage.

sentences.text: (d) On 06.10.2021, the respondent no.2, from her  mobile number, started blackmailing the family of  the revisionist/ petitioner and threatened the son of  revisionist to pay Rs.25.00 Lakhs, failing which, the  family of the revisionist will be implicated in a false  criminal case.

(e) On 25.10.2021, a settlement was executed through  the relatives Amit/ Devender Chaudhary and Sudhir  Kumar in their own handwriting with the  understanding of divorce of respondent no.1 with  son of revisionist on or after 22.03.2022, by mutual  consent.

(f) On 07.12.2021, when the revisionist was busy in his  legal profession, respondent no.2, from her mobile  number, called on his (revisionist) mobile number  extending threats to the revisionist and his family  and a complaint was also lodged in P.S. Tilak Marg  to that effect.

(g) The respondent no.2, for her unlawful gain, lodged  a frivolous FIR No. 84/2022 under Sections  354B/498A/323/506/511 IPC and Sections 3/4 of  the Dowry Prohibition Act at Mahila Thana,
 Muzaffar Nagar, U.P. against eight persons,
 including the revisionist.
(h) The revisionist got anticipatory bail vide order dated  07.06.2022.

(i) The son of revisionist namely Prashant sent a Legal  Notice dated 23.03.2022, in pursuance of the family  Understanding dated 25.10.2021.
The said Legal  Notice was not accepted by respondent no.2 and she  has also misbehaved with the revisionist and his son  during mediation proceedings on 26.05.2022.
The  son of revisionist has also filed HMA Petition  before the concerned Family Court.
(j) The revisionist has given complaints dated  26.05.2022, 18.09.2022, 19.09.2022, 25.10.2022  and 26.10.2022 to the concerned authorities.

3. Ld. counsel for the revisionist has relied upon the  following judgments:-

. As per the Action Taken Report filed by the police before  the Ld. Trial Court, it is submitted by the State that the  matter is a matrimonial dispute and in this regard,
 respondent no.2 has already lodged an FIR No. 84/2022  under Sections 376/354B/498A/323/506 and 511 IPC and  under Sections 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act at Mahila  Thana, Muzaffar Nagar, U.P.

It is further submitted that Crl. Rev. No. 159/2023 Jagbir Singh Malik Vs. NCT of Delhi Page - 4 of 6  regarding the incident dated 26.09.2021, since, the offence  was non-cognizable under Section 506 IPC, therefore,
 NCR no. 38/2021 under Section 506 IPC was registered at  P.S. Patparganj Industrial Area, Delhi against Vinod,
 Devender and Sudhir.

, it is submitted that the revisionist received the  threatening call at Patiala House Courts compound and as  per the submission of the revisionist, the complaint has  already been lodged at P.S. Tilak Marg.

It is also submitted  that regarding the incident dated 26.03.2022 that  mediation proceedings were occurred at Muzaffar Nagar,
 U.P. and the complainant/ revisionist may approach the  concerned police station at U.P.
The articles, alleged to  have been taken away by Ms. Preeti, also come under the  definition of 'Stridhan" and thus, no action is made out on  that part also.

6. The perusal of the bills of jewellery articles reveals that  the said articles are generally given to the bride at the time  of marriage by husband or her in-laws and as per law, the Jagbir Singh Malik vs Nct Of Delhi And Ors on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46538028/

Prima facie Section 406 IPC is not made out.

The  threatening complaints, at best, constitute offence under Section 506 IPC and the same are non-cognizable offence  and in one of the cases, NCR has already been lodged at  the concerned police station.
7. Settlement dated 25.10.2021, which was arrived at  between the family of respondent no.2 and revisionist  reveals that the same was done for a total sum of Rs.19.00  Lakhs.
In case, the settlement was not honoured, then, the Crl. Rev. No. 159/2023 Jagbir Singh Malik Vs. NCT of Delhi Page - 5 of 6

8. Considering the entire facts and circumstances of the  present case, prima facie no cognizable offence has been  made out.

Ld. Trial Court has already taken cognizance  under Section 200 Cr.P.C. and this Court is of the  considered view that there is no infirmity in the order  passed by Ld. Trial Court and as such, same does not call  for any interference.
FINAL ORDER:
9.

In view of the above observations, this Court is passing the  following final order:-
 ORDER (a) The present Revision Petition is hereby dismissed and accordingly, the impugned order dated 27.03.2023 is hereby upheld.
However, anything observed in this order shall have no bearings/expressions on the merits of the case.
(b) The copy of this order be placed with TCR and same be sent forthwith to the Ld. Trial Court for information.
File of Revision Petition be consigned to record room.
Announced in the open Court on this 16th day of October, 2023.

(ARUN SUKHIJA) Addl. Sessions Judge-03 (East) Karkardooma Courts: Delhi Crl. Rev. No.
